title: 1999 WRITE THE FUTURE - hella (˃̣̣̥╭╮˂̣̣̥) ✧ ♡ ‧º·˚
transcript: ﻿Here we have the debut full-length album from1999 WRITE THE FUTURE, an88rising-based, various artists collective who have strung together quite the feature list on this new LP here. You have everyone fromAmaaraetoBADBADNOTGOODtoGhostface KillahtoSouls of MischieftoBusta Rhymes, and alsoDel Tha Funkee Homosapien,The Budos Bandas well.

Even though there are some decent standout songs here and there, and it's very impressive that this roster of artists has been assembled and brought together for this type of record. What I think this album illustrates is the difficulty of directing projects like this, creatively speaking, because while there are a lot of impressive names on this album, the performances and songs tend to be spotty and inconsistent. In fact, it feels like a compilation of random mid-tier songs with little to no vision, pulling all of it together at the end of the day.

title: Civil Civic- "Run Overdrive" 7'' | REVIEW
whole_description:
Listen: http://theneedledrop.com/?p=32

BlogTV: http://www.blogtv.com/people/theneedledrop

AS Singles: http://theneedledrop.com/?p=137

On Civil Civic's new double b-side single, they break into some cleaner production and great textures. This is some highly visceral electrorock, with a blast of relentless fuzz that will leave your ears reeling in ecstacy. The tracks might not have hit me as hard as CC's first single, but they're both undeniably solid.

8/10 & 7/10

title: Devo- Something For Everybody | REVIEW
whole_description:
http://www.myspace.com/devo

This is Devo's first album in 20 years, and the band still has the same rigid, geeky rock energy that made their first albums so unique. At times, this band's shtick can wear thin with me, but the songs I do love on this LP are real heavy hitters. There were a few tracks I disliked, but it's still amazing to hear Devo back in the saddle.

6/10

title: Janelle Monáe- Archandroid | REVIEW
whole_description:
Listen: http://bit.ly/dtBhaM / http://bit.ly/cyafGJ

Ariel Pink w/Added Pizazz: http://theneedledrop.com/?p=148

On her full-length debut, Janelle Monae doesn't just hit out of the park. She goes all Dragon Ball Z and wallops it with the force of a thousand super saiyans. All animae references aside, this thing is great for dozens of reasons: immediate, conceptual, varied, and engaging. There's not a moment where I felt underwhelmed. The most out-of-place track has to be the Of Montreal collaboration on "Make the Bus," which isn't doing too much for me. Outside of that, I can't really say anything bad about this album. It's a revival of jazz, funk, and motown fundamentals with a contemporary kick. 

8/10 http://www.theneedledrop.com/loved-list/2010
